summary: An agent's ```mermaid block is drawn as a diagram and a ```chart block (a small versioned JSON spec: type bar, line or table, labels, named series of numbers, optional title and axis titles) as a chart, inside the chat on desktop, the Expo app and native Android. Only a closed top-level fence is drawn, so a block still streaming stays code; a block over 20,000 characters, an empty one or one past the twelfth in a message stays code. Each visual has a header with Source (raw text) and Copy (the SVG for a diagram, tab-separated data for a chart); the desktop adds Open in pane, which shows it at full size over the right pane while the terminal and IDE stay mounted underneath. An invalid chart or a diagram Mermaid cannot parse shows its error and its source. Mermaid is bundled (no network) and runs with securityLevel strict and HTML labels off; its SVG passes through DOMPurify, which removes scripts, event handlers, links, foreignObject and any url() outside the SVG. The desktop draws in the renderer, lazily when the block scrolls into view, with results cached by theme and source; charts use the theme variables. The phones load one bundled page (scripts/build-visual-host.mjs, committed as apps/mobile/assets/visual-host/visual-host.html) in a WebView that blocks navigation, file access and network loads, and send it the source as a JSON message. Agents learn the chart format from the Switchboard MCP server's instructions.

storageDataMigration.reason: Nothing is stored: the visuals are drawn from the message text already in the transcript, the pane visual is renderer state that is not persisted, and the render caches live in memory. Older and newer builds read the same messages; an older client shows the blocks as code.

The built visual host page was loaded in a hidden Electron window with its CSP: a flowchart, a sequence diagram and a chart drew through both answer paths (window.ReactNativeWebView and a MessagePort), a click directive and HTML in a label left no link or script, a parse error came back as an error, and no request left the page.
